ai_root_cause: PC-B is connected to VLAN 20 (Engineering) instead of VLAN 10 (Sales), preventing inter-VLAN communication on the same switch.

  Switch(config-if)# exit
  Switch(config)# end
  Switch# write memory
expected_fault: PC-B's port Fa0/6 is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of VLAN 10, so the two PCs are on different broadcast domains despite matching IP subnet config.

1. Switch(config)# interface fa0/9
2. Switch(config-if)# switchport mode access
3. Switch(config-if)# switchport access vlan 40
4. Verify with show interfaces fa0/9 switchport and test connectivity.
expected_fault: Port Fa0/9 is left in dynamic auto trunking mode instead of static access, causing intermittent DTP renegotiation and dropped frames after reboot.

ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool is misconfigured: it advertises the network 192.168.20.0/24 while the default router is set to 192.168.10.1, so clients cannot obtain a valid address and fall back to link‑local 169.254.x.x addresses.

expected_fault: The DHCP pool SALES-POOL is configured for the wrong network (192.168.20.0 instead of 192.168.10.0), so it never leases addresses to VLAN 10 clients, which fall back to APIPA.

ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool is configured with an exclusion range that consumes most of the address space (192.168.40.1-192.168.40.60) while the pool itself is 192.168.40.0/24. This leaves only 195 usable addresses, but the pool is already leasing 48 and a conflict was detected on 192.168.40.61. During peak usage the remaining addresses are exhausted or conflicted, causing intermittent DHCP failures for some PCs.
ai_evidence: show ip dhcp pool shows exclusion 1-60, 48 leased; show ip dhcp conflict shows 192.168.40.61 pinged; symptom of intermittent failures during rush.
ai_fix_steps: 1. Verify the intended address range and adjust the exclusion to free up more addresses (e.g., exclude only 192.168.40.1-192.168.40.10). 2. Ensure no static or manual assignments overlap the pool. 3. Restart the DHCP service or clear the conflict entry. 4. Monitor lease usage with "show ip dhcp binding" to confirm sufficient addresses.
expected_fault: The excluded-address range 192.168.40.1-192.168.40.60 combined with only /24 space leaves too few usable leases for the number of hosts, so the pool runs out during peak hours.

ai_root_cause: DHCP service is not enabled globally on R1, preventing the router from offering addresses to clients

ai_fix_steps:
1. Enter global configuration mode and issue "service dhcp" to enable DHCP on the router.
2. Verify that Gi0/0.30 is not excluded from DHCP relay (e.g., no "ip dhcp excluded-address" on that interface).
3. Reload or restart the DHCP service if necessary (e.g., "clear ip dhcp pool LAB-POOL").
4. Confirm clients receive IPs by checking the DHCP binding table with "show ip dhcp binding" and ensuring PCs obtain addresses.
expected_fault: The DHCP service is globally disabled ('no service dhcp'), so the router ignores all DISCOVER broadcasts regardless of the pool configuration.

ai_root_cause: DNS server 192.168.10.5 is unreachable from PC-F, causing name resolution failures; PC-F is also not configured with a DNS server address.

ai_fix_steps:
1. Verify that the DNS server 192.168.10.5 is up and reachable from the network segment.
2. On PC-F, configure the DNS server address: ipconfig /all (or set via network settings) to 192.168.10.5.
3. Test name resolution again with ping google.com or nslookup google.com.
4. If ping to 192.168.10.5 still fails, check the network path (e.g., ARP, gateway, routing) to identify connectivity issues.
expected_fault: PC-F has no DNS server configured (0.0.0.0), so name resolution fails while raw IP connectivity works fine - a classic Layer 7 vs Layer 3 split.

Then verify with "show services dns" to confirm it is On.

expected_fault: PC-H's secondary DNS entry duplicates the internal server instead of pointing to an external resolver, and the internal server has no forwarder configured, so external names can never be resolved.

ai_root_cause: The PC is configured with a static IP address and has not been assigned a DNS server address, so it cannot resolve hostnames.

or remove the final deny if appropriate

ai_root_cause: ACL 120 is applied inbound on Gi0/0.30 and denies all IP traffic, preventing VLAN 30 hosts from reaching the gateway or any other destination.

ai_root_cause: ACL 130 lacks a deny rule for Library-Guest traffic to the staff file server, allowing the traffic to pass.

Add a deny statement before the permit:
access-list 130 deny ip 192.168.55.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.50.20
access-list 130 permit ip 192.168.55.0 0.0.0.255 any
Then reload or apply the ACL again.
expected_fault: ACL 130 only contains a blanket permit for the guest subnet with no deny rule for the staff server, so the intended isolation between guest and staff networks was never actually implemented.

 ip nat inside
 exit
interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20

access-list 1 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255
ai_fix_steps:

2. Add an ACL entry to include the 192.168.20.0/24 network.
3. Verify NAT translations with 'show ip nat translations' and test connectivity from internal PCs.
expected_fault: The 'ip nat inside' designation was never applied to Gi0/0.10 (or any internal interface), so even though the NAT overload rule exists, the router doesn't know which interfaces are 'inside' to translate.

ai_root_cause: ACL 1 lacks a permit entry for the Sales VLAN 10 subnet (192.168.10.0/24), preventing NAT translation for that traffic
ai_evidence: show running-config | include access-list 1 displays only "access-list 1 permit 192.168.40.0 0.0.0.255" and no entry for 192.168.10.0/24
ai_fix_steps: Add the missing ACL rule: access-list 1 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255, then reload or apply the ACL to the NAT configuration

ai_root_cause: The NAT overload table on R1 is becoming saturated with dynamic translations, causing new connections to fail until the router is reloaded and the table is cleared.
ai_evidence: show ip nat statistics shows 0 active translations, peak 4096, expired 51200; show ip nat translations shows none; NAT overload is configured on a single ISP-facing interface with no static pool.
ai_fix_steps: Increase the NAT table size with 'ip nat translation table-size <value>' or reduce the idle timeout with 'ip nat timeout dynamic <seconds>' to allow more concurrent connections. Verify that the inside/outside interfaces are correctly configured with 'ip nat inside' and 'ip nat outside'.
expected_fault: The NAT translation table hit its peak capacity (4096) and expired entries aren't being cleared fast enough under load, exhausting available port/address combinations until a reload clears the table - a NAT overload capacity/timeout issue rather than a config typo.

ai_root_cause: The static NAT entry maps the public address 203.0.113.20 to the internal IP 192.168.50.3, but the library catalog server resides at 192.168.50.30. The mismatch prevents external connections from reaching the correct server.
ai_evidence: show running-config | include nat shows ip nat inside source static 192.168.50.3 203.0.113.20 and show ip nat translations lists 192.168.50.3 as the inside local address.
ai_fix_steps:
Update the static NAT entry to use the correct internal IP:
  ip nat inside source static 192.168.50.30 203.0.113.20
Then reload or apply the configuration and verify with show ip nat translations.
expected_fault: The static NAT entry points to 192.168.50.3 instead of the actual library server at 192.168.50.30 - a typo missing the trailing digit - so inbound connections are forwarded to the wrong (likely nonexistent) internal host.

ai_root_cause: The configured WPA2-PSK passphrase on the AP (C1sc0Secur3!) does not match the intended password (C1sc0Secure!), causing authentication failures.

rule_findings: [VLAN] VLAN 30 not found in VLAN database | [Trunk] VLAN 30 not in allowed-VLAN list on trunk Fa0/24 (allowed: 1,10,20)
ai_root_cause: VLAN 30 is not configured on SW2 and is not allowed on the trunk port Fa0/24, preventing wireless clients from receiving an IP address via DHCP.
ai_evidence: Rule engine findings: [VLAN] VLAN 30 not found in VLAN database | [Trunk] VLAN 30 not in allowed-VLAN list on trunk Fa0/24 (allowed: 1,10,20)
ai_fix_steps:
1. Configure VLAN 30 on SW2: 
   switch(config)# vlan 30
   switch(config-vlan)# name Lab-Wireless
   switch(config-vlan)# exit
2. Add VLAN 30 to the allowed list on trunk Fa0/24: 
   switch(config)# interface Fa0/24
   switch(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 30
   switch(config-if)# exit
3. Verify the VLAN appears in the VLAN database and the trunk allowed list. 4. Ensure the AP interface is mapped to VLAN 30 (already shown in AP3# show wlan summary). 5. Verify DHCP scope for VLAN 30 is active and reachable.
expected_fault: VLAN 30 is missing from the allowed-VLAN list on the AP's uplink trunk (Fa0/24 only allows 1,10,20), so wireless client traffic tagged for VLAN 30 is dropped at the switch and never reaches DHCP or the gateway.

ai_fix_steps: Increase the Max Clients value for the Library-WiFi SSID (e.g., to 30) or reduce the number of connected clients by deauthenticating unused stations or adding additional APs to distribute the load.
